Title: Russia says Putin received invitation to join Trump's 'Board of Peace'

Summary: 
Russian President Vladimir Putin has received an invitation to join the 'Board of Peace,' a proposed international body aimed at resolving conflicts, starting with the situation in Gaza, according to Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. Peskov confirmed the invitation was delivered through diplomatic channels and stated that Russia is currently reviewing the proposal, with hopes to clarify details through contact with the U.S. The White House announced the Board of Peace on January 15, 2026, describing it as central to implementing President Trump’s 20-point plan to end Israel’s war on Gaza, rebuild the enclave, provide strategic oversight, mobilize global resources, and ensure accountability during Gaza’s transition from conflict to peace and development. The U.S. also established the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), a founding Executive Board, and a Gaza Executive Board to support implementation. Trump has extended invitations to other global leaders, including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Title: Decision on joining Board of Peace after consultations with strategic partners: Putin

Summary: 
Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia's decision on joining the US-led Board of Peace, tasked with overseeing the Gaza ceasefire plan, will be made after consultations with Moscow’s strategic partners. In his televised remarks at the National Security Council meeting on January 22, 2026, Putin acknowledged the US administration’s efforts toward resolving the Ukrainian crisis and thanked US President Trump for the invitation. The Board of Peace, initially envisioned as a small group of world leaders for Gaza, has expanded under Trump’s vision to include dozens of nations and aims to mediate global conflicts, resembling a pseudo-UN Security Council. Putin emphasized that the core objective must be a long-term Palestinian-Israeli peace settlement based on UN resolutions, with due consideration for Palestinian needs—particularly reconstruction of Gaza’s infrastructure, healthcare, water supply, and food security. He announced a donation of USD 1 billion from Russian assets frozen under the previous US administration, before finalizing Russia’s participation. Putin also revealed plans to discuss the matter with Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas during Abbas’s two-day visit to Moscow, which began on January 21, 2026.

Published date: January 22 2026, 00:00

Title: Putin says he's considering 'Board of Peace' invite Trump claims was accepted

Summary: 
U.S. President Donald Trump claimed on January 21, 2026, that Russian President Vladimir Putin had accepted his invitation to join Trump's 'Board of Peace' initiative, a proposed global conflict resolution group. Trump made the statement during a press briefing at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, after meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. However, Putin quickly contradicted the claim, stating during a meeting with the Russian Security Council that the proposal was still under review by the foreign ministry and that no decision had been made. Trump justified the inclusion of controversial figures, including Putin, by asserting they possess 'tremendous influence' and 'get the job done.' The initiative aims to involve nations with powerful leaders in resolving global conflicts.

Title: Trump Invites Russia to Join Board of Peace

Summary: 
According to a guest post by Martin Armstrong published on January 20, 2026, Donald Trump has been named the first chairman of the newly established Board of Peace, formed in November 2025 to promote the Gaza-Israel ceasefire. Trump has begun inviting nations to join, including Russia. The article argues that the media's reaction to this initiative reflects a broader pattern: peace proposals are often opposed by those who benefit from conflict, as military and political institutions rely on an ongoing enemy for legitimacy, budgets, and relevance. Armstrong claims declassified Clinton-era documents show Russia was offered NATO membership in the 1990s, an offer rejected internally as a sign of submission, fueling domestic backlash in Russia. He contends that NATO’s expansion was not driven by necessity but by geopolitical profit and the desire for a unipolar world, which led to the permanent marginalization of Russia. The Board of Peace, Armstrong asserts, is a public relations effort to manage a global crisis fueled by sovereign debt, economic collapse in Europe, and the failure of fiscal policy. He argues that peace requires aligning interests, not moral posturing, and that integrating Russia into a broader security framework would remove the justification for escalation. He criticizes the West for hypocrisy, noting that if Russia had placed a military alliance near the U.S. border, the U.S. would respond similarly. Ultimately, Armstrong claims the current global hostility stems from a systemic cycle where governments resort to war when confidence in their economic and political systems collapses. He concludes that Trump’s vision threatens the entrenched war economy and exposes the long-standing lie that NATO was ever about defense rather than domination.

Published date: January 20 2026, 11:53

URL: https://www.theburningplatform.com/2026/01/20/trump-invites-russia-to-join-board-of-peace/
Source: The Burning Platform
Classification: Politics
Sentiment: negative
Reporting voice: Analytical
Continent: North America
